productAnchorNamed.chain: window.mainChart (host Chart) --_mcHostCacheFileRefOwners--> Map --__proto__--> Map.prototype --constructor--> closure Map --context--> <panel realm> NativeContext --global_object--> <panel realm> Window
productAnchorNamed.meaning: The host Chart's cache-file-ref-owner registry holds a Map that was CONSTRUCTED INSIDE a panel realm. Because the instance's prototype chain reaches that realm's Map constructor and therefore its NativeContext, holding the Map pins the panel's entire realm — and with it that realm's ~21 MB script set.
productAnchorNamed.shape: cross-realm container leak: a host-side registry storing an object built in the child realm
productAnchorNamed.cutForA: construct the registry's containers in the host realm and copy primitive keys across, and clear the entry on panel removal. The registry survives the panel, so anything realm-bound inside it is permanent.
productAnchorNamed.howFound: shortest-path BFS from GC roots over STRONG edges only — excluding 'weak' edges AND WeakMap key/value pairs, which the snapshot encodes as ordinary 'internal' edges. W77/W78's root path ((Eternal handles) -> FunctionTemplateInfo -> WeakMap) was such a non-retaining edge and is retracted as a retainer path.

instrumentCaveatMustBeRead.finding: In every snapshot examined (W78's and all three W79 runs), only 4 of the 12 peer realms are reachable from GC roots by product references: 2 are live root shortcuts and 2 go through _mcHostCacheFileRefOwners. The other 8 are reachable ONLY through '(Global handles) / DevTools console' — the inspector holding an Error whose 'get stack' accessor closes over that realm's context.
instrumentCaveatMustBeRead.consequence: Part of the per-cycle accumulation may be my own CDP session rather than the product. W78's 'one realm retained per cycle, 20.87 MB' is therefore NOT safe as stated: the mechanism (a whole realm's script set retained) is confirmed, the per-cycle RATE is now in question.
instrumentCaveatMustBeRead.attemptedRelease: Runtime.discardConsoleEntries + Runtime.releaseObjectGroup('console') before each floor sample. Both returned ok on all three cycles.
instrumentCaveatMustBeRead.result: NO EFFECT. Floors 105.30 / 131.83 / 152.61 (deltas +26.53, +20.78) against the control's 105.37 / 132.30 / 151.09 (+26.93, +18.79), and the snapshot still shows 4 product-held vs 8 console-only realms — identical to the control. The handles are not console entries and are not in the 'console' object group, so this ablation neither freed them nor settled the question.
instrumentCaveatMustBeRead.whyItMayExplainTheOvershoot: My rate is ~23 MB/cycle where the PO measures ~13 MB/cycle by hand with no automation. Inspector-held dead realms are a candidate explanation for exactly that ~10 MB/cycle overshoot. The PO's ~13 is unaffected by this and remains the product number.
instrumentCaveatMustBeRead.nextTestNamed: drive the cycles without evaluate-held exception objects (or with the Runtime domain torn down before the floor GC) and re-measure. If the rate falls toward the PO's ~13, the overshoot is mine and the product rate is the PO's.

constantOrRace.verdict: CONSTANT for B, RACE for the later peers
constantOrRace.evidence: B retained 3/3 cycles in four independent runs (control, worker-termination, console-release, dataset-rotation). C and D differ run to run and cycle to cycle: control {C:1,D:1}, worker-termination {C:2,D:1}, console-release {C:1,D:1}, rotation {D:2,C:0}.
